parameters.peer: Target conversation or account. Accepts "me"/"self", a supported username, a marked numeric ID already present in the peer cache, a full native entity, or a native InputPeer. User/channel IDs require a known access hash; basic group IDs do not. No access hash is guessed.
parameters.from_peer: Source conversation containing the original message IDs. Resolved independently from the destination peer. IDs are interpreted in this source chat.
parameters.peers: Nonempty sequence of user peers to remove from contacts. A string is not treated as a sequence of usernames. Each peer must resolve to an input user.
parameters.sender: Optional author filter for message search. None means do not restrict by author. When provided, the sender is resolved to an input user rather than a chat filter.
parameters.bot: Bot account whose inline results or start command are requested. Must resolve to a user peer; bot eligibility is enforced by Telegram.
parameters.phone: Phone number used by this operation. During login it identifies the account receiving a code; for contact operations it is contact data. Supply the international number explicitly; never log it.
parameters.code: Login code supplied by the user. Must be a nonempty string; it is sent once and never persisted. An incorrect code can be retried using the same saved challenge until Telegram expires it.
parameters.challenge: LoginChallenge returned by request_login_code or restored from client.login_challenge. None selects the checkpoint saved in this session. Do not mix challenges from different sessions or phones.
parameters.password: Current two-step-verification password. Used to compute an SRP proof off the event loop; the plain password is not written into session storage.
parameters.bot_token: Bot token to authorize instead of an interactive phone login. Mutually exclusive with phone. It is sensitive and must come from the application secrets mechanism.
parameters.max_attempts: Positive integer input budget for each interactive stage independently. Wrong phone/code/password inputs consume that stage budget. Flood waits, network failures, EOF and cancellation propagate without being treated as bad input.
parameters.prompts: LoginPrompts instance with async phone/code/password callbacks and a synchronous notify callback. None uses terminal input and hidden code/password prompts. Prompt exceptions propagate.
parameters.token: Sensitive bot token. Authorization is attempted once; invalid tokens do not start phone login. An already authorized session cannot be silently switched to another account.
parameters.authorization_hash: Signed integer hash from an Authorization returned by get_active_sessions. It identifies the remote authorization to terminate; it is not the auth-key bytes or the local session filename.
parameters.query_id: Signed 64-bit identifier from the relevant callback/inline query event. Use the value from that event; do not substitute a message ID or a random number.
parameters.text: Literal text for this operation. No implicit Markdown or HTML parser is applied. Pass explicit native entities where the signature supports them; unsupported parse_mode/formatting keywords are not accepted.
parameters.caption: Literal media caption. It is sent without implicit Markdown/HTML parsing. Empty text is allowed. The high-level media methods do not expose an entities argument.
parameters.reply_to: Optional positive message ID in the target conversation. None sends without a reply relationship. This is an integer high-level convenience, not a native InputReplyTo object. The valid high-level ID range is 1 through 2147483647; booleans are rejected.
parameters.silent: When True, requests silent delivery or a silent pin notification. It does not make content invisible, bypass permissions or guarantee that no recipient UI changes occur.
parameters.link_preview: Whether Telegram may generate a webpage preview. False becomes the native no_webpage flag. This does not parse formatting or upload a preview manually.
parameters.reply_markup: Native ReplyMarkup object, usually buttons.inline([...]) for an inline keyboard. None omits markup in the request. Editing omission is not a guaranteed instruction to remove existing markup; use an explicit supported raw operation when removal semantics matter.
parameters.entities: Explicit native MessageEntity objects. Entity offsets and lengths use Telegram UTF-16 code units, not Python string indices for non-BMP characters. None omits the optional field; an empty list explicitly supplies no entities.
parameters.limit: Total number of items to return across pages, not one RPC page size. Iterator methods accept None for unbounded traversal; list helpers require a finite nonnegative integer. Zero performs no pagination or peer resolution.
parameters.page_size: Per-request pagination batch size. Use 1–100 for dialogs/history/search and 1–200 for members. This does not change the total limit and does not enable background prefetch.
parameters.folder_id: Dialog folder selection. 0 is the main folder and 1 is the archive. Pinned dialogs are fetched separately and emitted first within the selected folder.
parameters.offset_id: Exclusive message-ID cursor for older history. 0 starts from the newest accessible messages. This is not a list index and is scoped to the target peer.
parameters.query: Search or inline-query text. Its interpretation depends on the selected operation. History search delegates matching to Telegram; no local regular-expression search is performed.
parameters.ids: A positive message ID or sequence of IDs. Up to 10,000 IDs are accepted and RPCs are chunked in batches of at most 100. Retrieval preserves order and duplicates; mutation batches can partially succeed.
parameters.message_id: Positive message ID scoped to the relevant conversation. For inline edits, this is instead a native InputBotInlineMessageID variant supplied by the inline callback, not a normal chat message ID. Ordinary message IDs must fit a positive signed-32-bit integer (1 through 2147483647).
parameters.revoke: Explicit request to remove messages for other participants where supported. Non-channel deletion validates all IDs against the target first. Channels always delete for everyone and therefore require revoke=True.
parameters.drop_author: Whether forwarding should hide the original author attribution using Telegram's supported flag. This is still a forward request and does not bypass source content protection.
parameters.max_id: Highest message ID to mark read. The high-level helper sends 0 unchanged when omitted; GramFlux does not invent a current maximum. Choose an explicit known ID when read scope matters.
parameters.callback: Previously registered async callback object. Registrations are removed by callback identity. Passing another function with the same name does not remove the original registration.
parameters.predicate: Synchronous composable Filter evaluated for the event type. Use &, | and ~ for composition. It must not block the event loop; it does not resolve usernames or fetch peers.
parameters.priority: Integer execution order: lower values run first; equal priorities preserve registration order. Handlers are awaited sequentially, not spawned without bounds.
parameters.edited: For on_message, False selects new messages and True selects edits. It does not subscribe to both variants; register both handlers or use on_edited_message explicitly.
parameters.event_type: One of the supported GramFlux event classes from gramflux.events. This selects the high-level event route before the predicate is evaluated; it is not a raw TL constructor class.
parameters.request: A GramFlux-generated native TL function object with definition.method=True. Constructor-only objects and foreign client objects are rejected. The raw result is returned without a high-level wrapper.
parameters.source: Path or seekable binary stream to upload. A stream starts at its current position. Library-owned path handles are closed; caller-owned streams remain open. Empty and nonseekable uploads are rejected.
parameters.file: Already uploaded InputFile/InputFileBig handle or supported native InputMedia object. This method does not accept a local path in place of a handle; use send_document/send_photo or upload_file first.
parameters.name: Optional transmitted filename. For uploads it overrides the inferred source name. It changes metadata, not the source path. Use a safe basename rather than embedding directory components.
parameters.on_progress: Optional callback called with (completed_bytes, total_bytes). It may be synchronous or return an awaitable. Upload progress counts completed part RPCs, not bytes merely read; callbacks can fail the operation and are not run as unbounded tasks.
parameters.part_size: Upload chunk size in bytes: a power of two from 1024 through 524288. Defaults to 512 KiB. Files are limited conservatively to 4000 parts; reducing this value can therefore reduce the maximum supported file size.
parameters.concurrency: Upload part-RPC window, integer 1–16. File reads stay sequential and at most this many parts are outstanding. This is not handler concurrency or download prefetch; higher values remain bounded by client request admission.
parameters.location: Native supported InputFileLocation, including inputDocumentFileLocation or inputPhotoFileLocation. It must carry current access hashes and file_reference data. A URL, filesystem path or Message is not an interchangeable location.
parameters.size: Known complete remote file size in bytes. Used to validate response lengths and byte ranges; it is not a maximum download budget. Supply current metadata rather than guessing.
parameters.offset: For downloads, zero-based byte position at which to start. Arbitrary range edges are aligned for the protocol and trimmed locally. For inline queries, this is instead the opaque pagination offset from BotResults.next_offset.
parameters.length: Optional number of bytes to return from offset. None requests the remaining file. Negative or out-of-bounds ranges are rejected instead of silently clamped; zero-length ranges make no file RPC.
parameters.request_size: Download request chunk size, a power of two from 4096 through 524288 bytes. It controls aligned network reads, not the exact application range. There is no speculative prefetch.
parameters.destination: New filesystem path or writable binary stream. Path targets never overwrite existing files and use a temporary sibling plus atomic finalization. Caller streams stay open and may retain partial bytes if the transfer fails.
parameters.message: Native Message containing supported document/photo metadata. GramFlux derives the remote location and size; unsupported media or stale references fail explicitly.
parameters.as_document: Whether an uploaded handle should be wrapped as a document rather than inferred photo media. This does not convert an arbitrary InputMedia object into another Telegram media kind.
parameters.mime_type: Optional MIME metadata for document media. None allows inference or the backend fallback. It is not a local file conversion or a content-validation promise.
parameters.alert: For callback answers, True requests an alert dialog instead of a brief notification. Only valid in the callback-answer flow; the server determines actual client behavior.
parameters.url: Optional callback-answer URL or a URL button destination. Must be a string where present; the high-level API does not bypass Telegram restrictions on games, domains or bot eligibility.
parameters.cache_time: Nonnegative signed-32-bit integer cache lifetime in seconds for the callback/inline response. 0 disables requested caching. This is unrelated to the local entity cache.
parameters.results: Sequence of native InputBotInlineResult objects, at most 50. IDs must be unique and each contain 1–64 UTF-8 bytes. Use buttons.article for a text article or construct native variants explicitly.
parameters.next_offset: Opaque pagination cursor returned to the caller of an inline query. An empty string indicates no next-page cursor; it is not an integer page number.
parameters.private: Requests per-user caching for inline results. This is a protocol cache-selection flag, not an access-control mechanism or a private-chat filter.
parameters.gallery: Requests gallery presentation for inline results. Actual rendering depends on result types and the Telegram client.
parameters.data: Callback payload bytes. get_callback_answer expects bytes; it does not encode strings automatically. Button builders and filters.data additionally accept strings and encode UTF-8.
parameters.game: Select the native game callback request behavior. It is a boolean flag and does not create or register a game.
parameters.commands: Sequence of at most 100 native BotCommand objects. Command names must be unique. Telegram enforces command naming/description rules and whether the account may manage the bot.
parameters.lang_code: Language selector for bot commands. Empty string requests the default language. This does not change the client's own interface language or translate descriptions.
parameters.scope: Native BotCommandScope. None selects BotCommandScopeDefault. Use a specific supported scope object for per-chat or other command sets rather than a string scope name.
parameters.action: Native SendMessageAction. None selects SendMessageTypingAction. Upload/recording actions may require fields such as progress; build the matching constructor explicitly.
parameters.top_message_id: Optional positive topic/thread root message ID for typing notifications. It is passed as top_msg_id; use the real topic root rather than the current message ID.
parameters.reactions: Emoji string, sequence of native Reaction objects, or None. A string becomes one ReactionEmoji. None or an empty sequence sends an empty reaction vector to remove the caller's reaction.
parameters.big: Whether Telegram should display the larger reaction animation. It changes presentation, not the reaction identity or account eligibility.
parameters.add_to_recent: Whether the reaction may be added to the account's recent reactions. It does not create a custom emoji or modify chat permissions.
parameters.expire_date: Optional future Unix timestamp for an exported invite. The helper accepts positive signed-32-bit values; Telegram decides whether the selected time is valid.
parameters.usage_limit: Optional positive signed-32-bit maximum number of joins for an invite. Cannot be combined with request_needed=True.
parameters.request_needed: Whether joining through the invite requires an administrator to approve a request. Cannot be combined with usage_limit.
parameters.invite_hash: Invite hash only, containing 1–256 ASCII letters, digits, underscore or hyphen. Do not pass an https://t.me/+ URL including its prefix.
parameters.title: Operation-specific title. For a chat it is the new chat name; for an invite it is the optional administrative label. Telegram applies its own length and permission rules.
parameters.description: Description text. For set_chat_description this is the chat's about field, and empty text clears it. For inline article results it is optional listing text, not the sent message body.
parameters.first_name: Nonempty first/display name for the profile or shared contact. It is literal metadata and does not resolve a username.
parameters.last_name: Last-name text. Empty string represents an empty value. In update_profile, None omits the field and keeps the existing value; empty string explicitly requests clearing it.
parameters.about: Profile biography/about text. None leaves the field unchanged; empty string requests clearing it. Telegram enforces allowed lengths.
parameters.share_phone: Explicit phone-privacy exception for the added contact. False does not opt the peer into seeing your number; True sets add_phone_privacy_exception. Treat this as a deliberate privacy choice.
parameters.start_param: Bot start payload, without a /start command prefix. It is sent through messages.startBot and is not executed as code by GramFlux.
parameters.vcard: Optional literal vCard metadata for a shared contact. Empty string omits useful vCard content; no address-book file is imported implicitly.
parameters.latitude: Finite real latitude in degrees from -90 through 90. Booleans, NaN and infinities are rejected.
parameters.longitude: Finite real longitude in degrees from -180 through 180. Booleans, NaN and infinities are rejected.
parameters.emoji: Dice/game emoji string for Telegram's InputMediaDice. Defaults to the dice emoji. Telegram validates supported emoji and generates the outcome; the caller cannot choose the result.
parameters.refresh: True forces fresh peer resolution and invalidates the old username binding. Cached names normally expire after 60 monotonic seconds and persisted names are not trusted after restart.
parameters.session: Explicit Session factory result, custom async Storage, path, or None. None uses memory. A bare path opens an existing authorized GramFlux session; use Session.create for new files and Session.open(..., require_authorized=False) for pending login.
parameters.api_id: Positive numeric Telegram application ID. Obtain it from your own application registration; it is not a bot ID or user ID.
parameters.api_hash: Application API hash containing exactly 32 hexadecimal characters. Pass it through an application secret mechanism; never log it.
parameters.config: Immutable Config instance. None constructs the documented defaults. Unknown Client keywords are not forwarded to a competitor library or socket implementation.
parameters.on_handler_error: Optional async callback (event, exception). Called for handler failures; redact exception contents yourself. Other eligible handlers continue unless propagation is explicitly stopped.
parameters.pattern: Regular-expression pattern compiled by Python re. It is matched against event text synchronously; use bounded/non-pathological patterns on untrusted input.
parameters.flags: Python re compilation flags such as re.IGNORECASE. This is unrelated to Telegram flags words or a count of filter matches.
parameters.names: One or more command names without a prefix, whitespace or @username suffix. The command filter inspects only the first token and does not parse or execute command arguments.
parameters.prefix: Nonempty command prefix matched at the start of the first token. The default slash is literal; it is not a regular-expression pattern.
parameters.username: Optional bot username without @. When supplied, addressed commands for another bot are rejected; without it an address for any username can match.
parameters.case_sensitive: When False, command names use casefold comparison. This does not change regex flags or normalize message content globally.
parameters.constructors: One or more native Update constructor classes, such as types.UpdateUserTyping. Pass classes, not instances or high-level event classes. They are validated against GramFlux's registry and combined as OR.
parameters.rows: Nonempty sequence of nonempty keyboard rows. Each row contains supported native inline KeyboardButton variants; reply-only phone/contact request buttons are rejected.
parameters.id: Inline result identifier string containing 1–64 UTF-8 bytes. Distinct results in one answer must have unique IDs. It is not a message ID.
parameters.value: Exact callback-data value as bytes or str. A string is encoded as UTF-8; this filter does not perform prefix, regex or JSON matching.
parameters.require_authorized: True requires the existing session to contain completed account authorization when connected. False allows an unfinished login file to be opened and resumed; it does not create a missing file.
parameters.address: Nonempty human-readable venue address. This is geographic display data, not a local filesystem output path or an account identifier.
parameters.anonymous: Whether poll votes should be anonymous. True omits public_voters; False requests public voter visibility subject to Telegram rules.
parameters.approve: True approves exactly the supplied pending join request; False dismisses it. This does not bulk-invite or join unrelated users.
parameters.correct_option: Optional zero-based index of the single correct quiz answer. None creates a normal poll; booleans/out-of-range indices and multiple-choice quizzes are rejected.
parameters.duration: Media duration in seconds supplied by the application. Video accepts finite nonnegative numeric seconds; audio/voice require nonnegative signed-32-bit integer seconds. No metadata is guessed.
parameters.forum: Whether the new megagroup should enable forum mode. Must be bool and is only exposed on supergroup creation, not automatic migration.
parameters.height: Actual frame height in pixels, supplied by the application. Must be a positive signed-32-bit integer; the helper does not decode video dimensions.
parameters.width: Actual frame width in pixels, supplied by the application. Must be a positive signed-32-bit integer; inaccurate encoded-file metadata remains a server/application error.
parameters.items: Sequence of 2–10 AlbumItem values. Use all photos or all documents; each item owns its source, literal caption, optional entities and document-mode flag.
parameters.link: Actual exported https://t.me/ invite URL. This is not a username, a guessed hash, or proof that your account may revoke it.
parameters.media: Native Photo, Document or ordinary Message carrying reusable server metadata. Protected Message inputs are rejected; opaque cross-library file-ID strings are not decoded.
parameters.multiple_choice: Whether a normal poll allows several answers. Must be bool; this helper rejects combining it with a single-answer correct_option quiz.
parameters.options: Sequence of 2–10 distinct nonempty option strings. Options become literal TextWithEntities values with client-generated option tokens, not shell or markup input.
parameters.performer: Optional literal audio performer metadata. None omits the field; it does not inspect tags in the source file or fetch an artist profile.
parameters.permissions: ChatPermissions describing allowed member actions. False becomes the corresponding forbidden Telegram right; this object never grants administrator privileges.
parameters.photos: Sequence of 1–100 native Photo/InputPhoto values with real server IDs, access hashes and file references. Integer IDs alone are not sufficient.
parameters.privileges: AdminPrivileges describing explicit administrator grants. All defaults are False; an all-false value removes admin grants rather than requesting every permission.
parameters.provider: Optional venue provider label supplied by the application. Empty means no provider metadata; it does not trigger a third-party place lookup.
parameters.question: Nonempty literal poll question. This helper creates TextWithEntities with an empty entity list rather than parsing Markdown or HTML implicitly.
parameters.rank: Optional literal administrator rank. Empty omits the field; Telegram enforces rank length, character constraints and the caller's grant authority.
parameters.result_id: Nonempty opaque inline-result ID from a real get_inline_bot_results response, at most 64 UTF-8 bytes. It is not an ordinary message ID.
parameters.short_name: Registered bot game short name. Supply it with an accessible bot reference; the helper neither registers games nor invents game identifiers.
parameters.solution: Optional quiz explanation, at most 200 Python characters and two newline characters. Requires correct_option; matching empty solution_entities is encoded with the shared flag.
parameters.supports_streaming: Whether the supplied MP4 is suitable for streaming. Must be bool; setting the flag does not convert the file or move its metadata atoms.
parameters.until_date: Nonnegative signed-32-bit Unix timestamp for restrictions. Zero is the permanent sentinel. This is not a relative seconds duration; Telegram determines expiry/permanent interpretation.
parameters.user: User/member reference resolved through the existing account-local peer policy. No access hash is invented; default menu scope uses None only where explicitly documented.
parameters.users: Sequence of 1–200 accessible user references for basic-group creation. Resolution does not override invite/privacy restrictions or prove every invitee can be admitted.
parameters.venue_id: Optional provider-specific place identifier. Empty leaves provider identification unspecified; this does not resolve an external location database automatically.
parameters.venue_type: Optional provider-specific category/type string for the venue. It is independent from the geographic coordinates and destination conversation.
parameters.waveform: Optional server-format waveform bytes for a voice note. A string is rejected; no waveform generation, audio decoding or file transcoding is performed.

overrides.iter_members.query: Participant-name search passed to the channel participant search filter. Empty string lists accessible members. Basic-group participants are obtained from full-chat metadata, so the same server search semantics are not promised.
overrides.get_members.query: Participant-name search where supported by the channel endpoint. Empty string requests accessible members; this is not an arbitrary message query.
overrides.get_callback_answer.message_id: Positive integer ID of the message whose callback button is being invoked, scoped to peer.
overrides.edit_inline_message.message_id: Native InputBotInlineMessageID or InputBotInlineMessageID64 from an inline callback. This is neither a regular integer message ID nor a string copied from another library.
overrides.get_inline_results.offset: Opaque cursor from a previous BotResults.next_offset. Empty string starts the first page; do not parse or increment it as an integer.
overrides.add_contact.phone: Optional contact phone metadata. Empty string is accepted. This is not a login request and does not request an authorization code.
overrides.save_draft.text: Literal draft content; empty string is allowed to clear a draft. There is no automatic Markdown/HTML parsing.
overrides.answer_callback_query.text: Notification/alert text. Empty string acknowledges without text; empty text is omitted from the optional native message field.
overrides.edit_inline_message.text: Literal replacement inline-message text. This helper accepts empty text at local validation; Telegram determines whether the final edit is valid.
overrides.set_chat_title.title: Nonempty replacement basic-group or channel/supergroup title. A user account peer is not a valid target.
overrides.export_invite_link.title: Optional administrative title for the exported invite. None omits the field; it is not the destination chat title.
overrides.get_history.offset_id: Exclusive message-ID cursor for fetching messages older than this ID. 0 starts from the newest accessible history; no time/date conversion is performed.
overrides.update_profile.first_name: Optional new first name. None leaves it unchanged; an explicitly supplied value must be nonempty.
overrides.filters.chat.ids: One or more marked numeric chat IDs matched against event.chat_id. User IDs are positive, basic groups negative, channels -(1000000000000 + channel_id). No network lookup is done.
overrides.filters.sender.ids: One or more numeric sender IDs compared with event.sender_id. Events lacking sender information fail the predicate. Usernames are not resolved.
overrides.buttons.callback.text: Nonempty visible button label. This is not callback payload and is not parsed as Markdown.
overrides.buttons.callback.data: Payload bytes or UTF-8 text, exactly 1–64 encoded bytes. Keep it compact; do not put passwords or other secrets into a publicly reachable callback payload.
overrides.buttons.url.url: Nonempty URL string used by the native URL button. The builder does not fetch or validate the remote resource; Telegram applies URL/domain restrictions.
overrides.buttons.article.title: Visible article-result title. The sent text comes from the separate text argument.
overrides.buttons.article.text: Literal text that will be sent when the article is chosen. It is not a description label; supply explicit native MessageEntity objects for formatting.
overrides.Session.open.name: Existing GramFlux session name or path. A name without a suffix gets .session. The parent/file must exist; creation is not implied.
overrides.Session.create.name: New GramFlux filename or name, with .session added when no suffix exists. The parent directory must exist. An existing path is never replaced.

overrides.edit_folder.peers: Sequence of 1–100 conversation references to move between main and archive. Each is resolved through the existing peer policy; this is not a custom dialog-filter definition.
overrides.edit_folder.folder_id: Integer 0 selects the main conversation list and 1 selects archive. Booleans, floats and other folder IDs are rejected; custom filters are a separate workflow.
overrides.send_video_note.length: Actual square video-note frame side in pixels. Must be a positive signed-32-bit integer; this field is unrelated to a download byte-range length.
overrides.send_audio.title: Optional literal audio track title. None omits the audio attribute field; it is not a chat title update or metadata extracted from the source.
overrides.edit_message_media.caption: Optional new literal caption. None omits text editing; an explicit string edits the caption and clears explicit entities. It is not an implicit Markdown input.
overrides.set_chat_menu_button.commands: True selects Telegram's bot commands menu; False with no Web App fields selects the default menu. Cannot be combined with text or URL.
overrides.set_chat_menu_button.text: Nonempty Web App menu button label, paired with a HTTPS URL. None selects a commands/default button according to the commands flag.
overrides.set_chat_menu_button.url: HTTPS Web App destination paired with nonempty text. Both fields must be supplied together; no redirect fetching or external HTTP download occurs.
overrides.set_chat_menu_button.user: Optional accessible user reference for a per-user bot menu. None deliberately uses InputUserEmpty for the default user scope, not the current user.
overrides.get_chat_menu_button.user: Optional accessible user reference whose bot menu should be read. None selects the server default user scope and does not guess an account ID.

overrides.iter_admin_log.max_id: Exclusive upper admin-log event ID, a nonnegative signed-64-bit integer. Zero starts at the newest accessible event; this is not a message-read cursor.
overrides.send_sticker.emoji: Literal alternative sticker emoji metadata, empty by default. This does not select a dice outcome, create a sticker pack, or convert the source file format.

overrides.send_media.as_document: False sends photo media; True sends a document with filename metadata. This selects the input-media constructor without converting encoded file content.
overrides.edit_message_media.as_document: False replaces with photo media; True replaces with generic document media. This chooses the input constructor and does not inspect or convert the file.
overrides.send_venue.title: Nonempty literal venue name shown beside the geographic address. It is not a chat rename or an invite administrative label.
overrides.send_inline_bot_result.query_id: Signed-64-bit query identity from the real BotResults returned by get_inline_bot_results. Use its associated result ID, not an incoming inline-event ID or a message identifier.
overrides.get_participants.query: Member-name search text passed to the existing get_members service. Channel search and basic-group filtering retain their existing behavior; no history message search is performed.
overrides.create_channel.about: Literal description for the newly created channel/supergroup. Empty creates it without description; None is not accepted and there is no existing description to preserve.
overrides.create_supergroup.about: Literal description for the newly created channel/supergroup. Empty creates it without description; None is not accepted and there is no existing description to preserve.
overrides.get_admin_log.query: Literal server-side administrative log search query. Empty requests unfiltered visible events; it is not a message-history search or local regular expression.
overrides.iter_admin_log.query: Literal server-side administrative log search query. Empty requests unfiltered visible events; it is not a message-history search or local regular expression.
overrides.search_messages_count.sender: Optional author reference resolved to an InputPeer for Telegram message search. None omits this restriction; user/channel access metadata follows the existing resolver policy.

connect.summary: Open storage, restore native session metadata, establish the MTProto connection and start update dispatch. Does not prompt for account login.
notes: A completed saved authorization is checked only when the session factory requires it. Calling connect on an already connected client is a no-op; a broken backend requires disconnect before reconnecting.

disconnect.summary: Cancel and join outstanding requests and callbacks, stop native update production, close the transport and save the session snapshot.
notes: Use from the main task, not from an event handler. Cancelling disconnect does not abandon its cleanup worker. It is not remote logout.

is_authorized.summary: Ask Telegram whether this authorization key is attached to an authorized account.
is_authorized.returns: bool; True also clears stale pending-login metadata.
notes: A socket being connected or a key being present is not sufficient evidence of account authorization.

login.summary: Explicitly run bounded interactive user login, authorize a bot token, or return the already authorized user.
notes: Saved code/password checkpoints are resumed when appropriate. phone and bot_token are mutually exclusive. Repeated interactive login calls are serialized; do not run other authentication primitives concurrently.

request_login_code.summary: Request a Telegram login code and commit its phone/code-hash checkpoint before returning.
request_login_code.returns: LoginChallenge; may raise PasswordRequired after saving the password stage.
notes: Does not resubmit wrong inputs. Calling it again requests a new challenge. The existing session must not already be authorized.

sign_in.summary: Submit a login code using an explicit or saved challenge and persist completed authorization.
notes: PasswordRequired is saved before propagating, allowing another process to supply the password later. Wrong codes retain progress; expired or invalidated hashes clear it. No challenge raises LifecycleError.

check_password.summary: Fetch fresh SRP parameters, compute the proof off-loop and finish two-step account authorization.
notes: A wrong password leaves the password checkpoint retryable. The plain password is not stored. Already authorized accounts are not replaced.

sign_in_bot.summary: Authorize a bot account once with its token and persist the resulting authorization.
notes: Use a separate session for another account. A wrong token propagates; it never falls back to asking for a phone number.

log_out.summary: Explicitly revoke the current remote authorization, clear local key/cache metadata and disconnect.
log_out.returns: None only after a confirmed LoggedOut response.
notes: The Client cannot reconnect afterward. Local temporary-session cleanup does not call this automatically. A lost reply can leave the remote outcome uncertain.

get_me.summary: Fetch the current authorized account identity.
notes: An unauthorized account raises AuthenticationRequired. This method does not start login.

resolve_peer.summary: Resolve a supported peer representation into a native input peer without inventing access hashes.
notes: Marked IDs use positive users, negative basic groups and -(1000000000000 + channel_id) channels. Unknown user/channel IDs need metadata from an accessible entity.

get_chat.summary: Fetch the current basic entity for a supported peer and update peer metadata.
notes: This is basic entity data, not the full profile/participant response. Use get_chat_full or get_user_full for those endpoints.

get_user.summary: Fetch a basic entity and require it to be a user.
notes: A group/channel peer raises ConfigurationError rather than returning another entity kind.

get_user_full.summary: Request the full Telegram user profile for a user peer.
notes: Requires a user input peer. Availability of fields still depends on Telegram privacy rules.

get_chat_full.summary: Request full basic-group or channel/supergroup metadata using the appropriate endpoint.
notes: User peers are not a substitute for group/channel peers. Hidden or forbidden metadata is not bypassed.

get_contacts.summary: Fetch the current complete contacts response with a zero cache hash.
notes: An unexpected not-modified response raises PaginationError rather than pretending an empty list is complete.

block_user.summary: Block a resolved user through the contacts API.
notes: Requires a user peer; it is not a channel moderation ban.

unblock_user.summary: Remove a block on a resolved user.
notes: This does not re-add a deleted contact or restore old messages.

add_contact.summary: Add a resolved user to contacts with explicit name and phone-sharing choices.
notes: first_name cannot be empty. share_phone=True changes a privacy exception; it must be a real boolean.

delete_contacts.summary: Remove the selected user contacts from the account.
notes: The sequence must not be empty. This does not delete message history or block those accounts.

update_profile.summary: Update only explicitly supplied name/biography fields for the current user.
notes: At least one field must be supplied. None means unchanged; empty last_name/about clears that field. An explicitly empty first_name is rejected.

get_active_sessions.summary: List Telegram authorizations attached to the current account.
notes: These remote account authorizations are different from local SQLite session filenames.

terminate_session.summary: Revoke the specific remote authorization identified by its hash.
notes: Inspect get_active_sessions first. The hash is not an auth-key ID, and Telegram can impose account-age/security restrictions.

send_message.summary: Send nonempty literal text, optionally with a reply, explicit entities and native keyboard markup.
send_message.returns: Native Message normalized from the server response.
notes: No parse_mode or arbitrary **kwargs are accepted. Telegram limits and entity UTF-16 offsets apply. A lost response is not automatically resent with a new random ID.

edit_message.summary: Edit nonempty literal message text in a known peer.
edit_message.returns: Native Updates result, not a replacement Message.
notes: This helper supplies an empty entities vector and exposes no entities/reply_markup parameter. Use edit_inline_message for inline IDs, or a raw request for additional supported TL options.

delete_messages.summary: Delete validated IDs from an explicitly selected conversation.
delete_messages.returns: list of messages.AffectedMessages results, one per batch.
notes: All non-channel IDs are preflight-checked for chat scope before any delete. Channel deletion always affects everyone and requires revoke=True. Multi-batch operations are not atomic.

forward_messages.summary: Forward messages from an explicit source peer into a destination peer with independent secure random IDs.
forward_messages.returns: list of native Updates, one per batch.
notes: IDs are scoped to from_peer. Telegram content-protection and permissions apply. A later batch failure does not roll back earlier forwards.

read_history.summary: Mark history as read using the user/group or channel endpoint.
read_history.returns: AffectedMessages for users/basic groups; bool for channels.
notes: The helper sends max_id unchanged. It is not a durable acknowledgement of application callback processing.

pin_message.summary: Pin a message in the selected conversation.
notes: The default requests a silent pin. Telegram decides whether this account may pin in the conversation.

unpin_message.summary: Unpin the selected message in its conversation.
notes: This is a targeted unpin, not an unpin-all operation.

iter_dialogs.summary: Create a lazy iterator over pinned dialogs followed by regular dialogs in one folder.
iter_dialogs.returns: AsyncIterator of Dialog records; do not await the iterator factory.
iter_dialogs.example:
async for dialog in client.iter_dialogs(limit=200, folder_id=0, page_size=50):
    print(dialog.id)
notes: Only the next page is requested on demand. Missing/stalled cursors raise PaginationError. No snapshot transaction or durable deduplication is promised.

get_dialogs.summary: Materialize a finite collection of dialogs using the lazy iterator.
notes: limit=None is not accepted. For large traversals use iter_dialogs to avoid retaining the entire collection.

iter_history.summary: Lazily traverse accessible messages newest first, starting before offset_id when supplied.
iter_history.example:
async for message in client.iter_history("me", limit=200, page_size=50):
    print(message.id)
notes: The factory is not awaitable. Short pages do not incorrectly end sliced history; cursors must advance.

get_history.summary: Collect a finite newest-first message history.
notes: The list is held in memory. limit is total output, not the server request size.

iter_search.summary: Lazily search one conversation through Telegram, optionally restricting the author.
iter_search.example:
async for message in client.iter_search("me", "meeting", limit=100):
    print(message.id)
notes: The query is not a local regex. Sender filtering requires a user peer. Results can change while pagination is running.

search_messages.summary: Collect a finite set of server-side search results in one peer.
notes: None is not a valid list limit. Use iter_search for lazy traversal or sender-specific searching without retaining all output.

get_messages.summary: Retrieve explicit IDs while preserving requested order and duplicate IDs.
get_messages.returns: list of Message/MessageService or None per requested ID.
notes: Missing, deleted or other-chat results become None. A single ID still returns a list, not one Message.

iter_members.summary: Lazily enumerate accessible basic-group or channel/supergroup participants.
iter_members.example:
async for member in client.iter_members(group_peer, limit=100, page_size=50):
    print(member.id, member.role)
notes: Bots/users see only what Telegram permits. Hidden/forbidden participant lists do not become fabricated empty complete lists.

get_members.summary: Materialize a finite list of accessible participant records.
notes: Records can have user=None when the entity table lacks full user information. limit=None is not accepted.

join_chat.summary: Join a resolved public channel/supergroup through its channel endpoint.
notes: This is an explicit membership change. Resolving a peer does not join it; use import_invite for a private invite hash.

leave_chat.summary: Leave a basic group or a channel/supergroup using the corresponding endpoint.
notes: This does not delete a private user dialog. Telegram can prevent leaving under method-specific restrictions.

import_invite.summary: Attempt to join through a private invite hash.
notes: Pass only the hash, not a URL. Joining can require approval or fail because the invite expired; check_invite is a separate inspection operation.

check_invite.summary: Inspect an invite hash without calling the join endpoint.
notes: Inspect the returned constructor: it can represent different invite/account membership states. This method does not join automatically.

export_invite_link.summary: Create/export a chat invite with explicit expiry, usage and approval choices.
notes: expiry/usage values must be positive signed-32-bit integers. request_needed and usage_limit cannot be combined. Administrative permission is enforced by Telegram.

set_chat_title.summary: Change a basic group or channel/supergroup title using the appropriate endpoint.
notes: Requires a nonempty string and suitable account permissions. A user peer is not a valid target.

set_chat_description.summary: Set or clear a chat about/description field.
notes: Empty description requests clearing. Chat permissions and server-side length limits remain authoritative.

invoke.summary: Execute a native GramFlux-generated TL function object through the shared request engine.
invoke.returns: Actual decoded native result, list or primitive.
notes: No implicit high-level peer resolution or arbitrary retry is added. A constructor that is not a method raises TypeError. Raw declaration availability does not implement unsupported workflows.

run_until_disconnected.summary: Wait for backend disconnection while allowing other asyncio tasks to run.
run_until_disconnected.returns: None for normal disconnection; backend failure is re-raised.
notes: The client must already be connected. Cancelling this waiter does not cancel the backend disconnected future or silently disconnect unrelated work.

upload_file.summary: Read a local binary source in order and submit a bounded number of upload parts.
upload_file.returns: InputFile for files up to 10 MiB, otherwise InputFileBig.
notes: At most 4000 parts are supported. Caller streams remain open. Empty uploads are rejected. The return value is a handle, not a sent message.

send_file.summary: Send a local path/stream, uploaded handle or supported native media through the existing upload and send pipeline.
notes: Local sources are uploaded with existing default chunk/window settings. JPG/JPEG/PNG paths infer photo mode unless document mode/MIME is explicit. Uploaded handles retain their previous behavior; uploads and sends are not an atomic transaction.

send_document.summary: Upload a source, then send the uploaded result as a document.
notes: Upload success alone does not prove the final message was sent. A later send failure can leave an uploaded handle on the server. Partial remote outcomes are not retried automatically.

send_photo.summary: Upload a source, explicitly wrap it as photo media, then send it.
notes: This is not a document fallback or image-conversion service. Unsupported/corrupt image data is rejected by Telegram.

iter_download.summary: Create a lazy iterator yielding exactly the requested byte range from a native remote location.
iter_download.returns: AsyncIterator of bytes; the factory itself is not awaited.
iter_download.example:
async for block in client.iter_download(location, size=size, offset=0, length=8192):
    consume(block)
notes: Requests are aligned and trimmed, limited to a protocol window, and response lengths are validated. There is no prefetch, CDN fallback, reference refresh or resumable-transfer state.

iter_download_media.summary: Resolve supported document/photo metadata from a message and yield its requested byte range.
iter_download_media.example:
async for block in client.iter_download_media(message, offset=0, length=8192):
    consume(block)
notes: Use async for directly. Native message metadata supplies full size; unsupported media raises explicitly rather than guessing a location.

download_file.summary: Stream an exact range to a new path or caller-owned binary output stream.
download_file.returns: Path for a path destination; None for a caller stream.
notes: A path target never overwrites an existing file. Failed/cancelled path transfers remove their temporary file; caller streams can retain partial data.

download_media.summary: Resolve a supported message's media location and size, then stream an exact range.
download_media.returns: Path for a path destination; None for a caller stream.
notes: Only supported document/photo metadata is resolved. Cross-DC media/CDN redirects and expired-reference recovery remain unsupported.

answer_callback_query.summary: Answer an incoming bot callback query with notification text, an alert, or a permitted URL.
notes: Use the query ID from the event rather than its message ID. Telegram can reject expired queries or disallowed URL/game contexts.

answer_inline_query.summary: Publish at most 50 native inline results with explicit caching and pagination choices.
notes: Result IDs must be unique and 1–64 UTF-8 bytes. This does not configure inline mode for the bot; Telegram configuration and account eligibility still apply.

edit_inline_message.summary: Edit the text/markup of an inline bot message by its native inline identifier.
notes: A normal integer message ID is not accepted by the protocol. None markup omits that optional field; use an explicit native markup when replacing it.

get_inline_results.summary: Request inline results from a bot for a query and target peer context.
notes: The bot input must be a user. This retrieves results; it does not choose and send one of them.

get_callback_answer.summary: Invoke a message's supported callback payload and receive the bot answer.
notes: data must be bytes if supplied. This is the user-side callback invocation, unlike answer_callback_query which answers a bot event.

set_bot_commands.summary: Replace a bot command list for a selected native scope and language.
notes: The list may contain at most 100 unique command names. Empty commands can clear that command set. None scope maps to BotCommandScopeDefault.

get_bot_commands.summary: Read the command list for a selected scope/language pair.
notes: The default language is empty string and the default scope is global. This does not merge all scopes into one list.

set_typing.summary: Send a native typing or other SendMessageAction notification, optionally in a topic.
notes: A default None action becomes typing. This sends once; GramFlux does not start a repeating background typing task.

send_reaction.summary: Set, replace or remove the current account's reaction on a message.
notes: None/[] removes the caller's reactions. Native Reaction objects permit variants beyond a simple emoji, subject to account and chat limits.

save_draft.summary: Set or clear a literal draft in one conversation with optional reply context.
notes: Empty text is allowed for clearing. This stores a server-side draft; it does not send a message or expose every raw saveDraft option.

start_bot.summary: Start a bot with an explicit target peer and start payload.
notes: GramFlux assigns a secure random ID. This is a user-side bot-start operation, not authorization of the bot token.

send_contact.summary: Send a contact card built from literal phone/name/vCard fields.
notes: phone and first_name must be nonempty. This shares contact data; it does not add the recipient to your address book automatically.

send_location.summary: Send a static geographic point with validated finite coordinates.
notes: Only a static point is exposed here. Live-location period, accuracy, venue and heading parameters require an appropriate raw workflow.

send_dice.summary: Send a Telegram-generated dice/game media object.
notes: The caller chooses an allowed emoji, not the random outcome. Unsupported emoji/account behavior is decided by Telegram.

on_message.summary: Register an async callback for new messages; edited=True selects edits.
on_message.returns: Decorator returning the original callback; the callback receives MessageEvent.
notes: Register before connecting. Callbacks run sequentially with bounded queues; lower priority executes first. Handler failures are reported and isolated. Use a shutdown signal to the main task rather than disconnecting inside the handler.

on_edited_message.summary: Register an async callback for edited messages only.
on_edited_message.returns: Decorator returning the original callback; the callback receives MessageEvent.
notes: Register before connecting. Callbacks run sequentially with bounded queues; lower priority executes first. Handler failures are reported and isolated. Use a shutdown signal to the main task rather than disconnecting inside the handler.

on_raw_update.summary: Register an async callback for accepted native Update objects, without fabricated wrappers for difference.new_messages.
on_raw_update.returns: Decorator returning the original callback; the callback receives RawUpdateEvent.
notes: Register before connecting. Callbacks run sequentially with bounded queues; lower priority executes first. Handler failures are reported and isolated. Use a shutdown signal to the main task rather than disconnecting inside the handler.

on_deleted_messages.summary: Register an async callback for message deletions; global non-channel deletions may not identify a chat.
on_deleted_messages.returns: Decorator returning the original callback; the callback receives DeletedMessagesEvent.
notes: Register before connecting. Callbacks run sequentially with bounded queues; lower priority executes first. Handler failures are reported and isolated. Use a shutdown signal to the main task rather than disconnecting inside the handler.

on_read_history.summary: Register an async callback for read-history changes with max_id and inbox/outbox direction.
on_read_history.returns: Decorator returning the original callback; the callback receives ReadHistoryEvent.
notes: Register before connecting. Callbacks run sequentially with bounded queues; lower priority executes first. Handler failures are reported and isolated. Use a shutdown signal to the main task rather than disconnecting inside the handler.

on_user_status.summary: Register an async callback for user status changes, subject to Telegram privacy and visibility.
on_user_status.returns: Decorator returning the original callback; the callback receives UserStatusEvent.
notes: Register before connecting. Callbacks run sequentially with bounded queues; lower priority executes first. Handler failures are reported and isolated. Use a shutdown signal to the main task rather than disconnecting inside the handler.

on_chat_action.summary: Register an async callback for native service messages describing supported chat actions.
on_chat_action.returns: Decorator returning the original callback; the callback receives ChatActionEvent.
notes: Register before connecting. Callbacks run sequentially with bounded queues; lower priority executes first. Handler failures are reported and isolated. Use a shutdown signal to the main task rather than disconnecting inside the handler.

on_callback_query.summary: Register an async callback for bot callback queries; inline identifiers are distinct from ordinary message IDs.
on_callback_query.returns: Decorator returning the original callback; the callback receives CallbackQueryEvent.
notes: Register before connecting. Callbacks run sequentially with bounded queues; lower priority executes first. Handler failures are reported and isolated. Use a shutdown signal to the main task rather than disconnecting inside the handler.

on_inline_query.summary: Register an async callback for bot inline queries carrying query text and pagination offset.
on_inline_query.returns: Decorator returning the original callback; the callback receives InlineQueryEvent.
notes: Register before connecting. Callbacks run sequentially with bounded queues; lower priority executes first. Handler failures are reported and isolated. Use a shutdown signal to the main task rather than disconnecting inside the handler.

on.summary: Register an async callback for instances of the selected supported high-level event type.
on.returns: Decorator returning the original callback; the callback receives selected event class.
notes: Register before connecting. Callbacks run sequentially with bounded queues; lower priority executes first. Handler failures are reported and isolated. Use a shutdown signal to the main task rather than disconnecting inside the handler.

off_event.summary: Remove all registrations associated with the same callback object.
notes: Removal affects subsequent dispatch snapshots. An already selected in-flight handler is not retroactively cancelled. Keep the original decorated callback object if you need to unsubscribe it.

off_message.summary: Remove all registrations associated with the same callback object.
notes: Removal affects subsequent dispatch snapshots. An already selected in-flight handler is not retroactively cancelled. Keep the original decorated callback object if you need to unsubscribe it.

__init__.summary: Construct an asyncio-first client with explicit session intent, application credentials, immutable settings and an optional handler-error reporter. Construction does not connect or prompt.
__init__.returns: A Client instance; use it on one asyncio event loop.
notes: Use Session.create only once for a new filename. For an unfinished login use Session.open(..., require_authorized=False). A bare path means open an existing authorized session. Unknown constructor keywords are rejected.

approve_chat_join_request.summary: Approve or dismiss one pending join request without bulk admission.
notes: The account needs Telegram permission to manage join requests. This does not invite arbitrary users.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

ban_chat_member.summary: Ban a peer from viewing a supergroup/channel until an explicit server timestamp.
notes: Channel/supergroup only. Zero is the permanent-ban sentinel; timestamps are Unix seconds, not relative durations.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

unban_chat_member.summary: Clear a supergroup/channel member ban and restriction flags.
notes: Clearing flags does not re-add the user. This also clears individual restrictions, not only the view ban.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

restrict_chat_member.summary: Apply explicit allowed-action settings to a supergroup/channel member.
restrict_chat_member.example:
from gramflux import ChatPermissions
await client.restrict_chat_member(channel_peer, user_peer, ChatPermissions(send_messages=False))
notes: ChatPermissions uses positive allowed actions and translates them to forbidden Telegram flags. Basic groups are not silently upgraded.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

promote_chat_member.summary: Set explicit administrator grants and an optional rank for a channel member.
promote_chat_member.example:
from gramflux import AdminPrivileges
await client.promote_chat_member(channel_peer, user_peer, AdminPrivileges(delete_messages=True), rank="Moderator")
notes: All-false AdminPrivileges demotes. Ownership, grant restrictions and account eligibility are server enforced.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

set_chat_permissions.summary: Set default group member permissions using a positive high-level settings object.
set_chat_permissions.example:
from gramflux import ChatPermissions
await client.set_chat_permissions(group_peer, ChatPermissions(send_media=False))
notes: These are default member restrictions, not admin grants. True means allowed; no rights are inferred from local membership.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

copy_message.summary: Copy accessible ordinary text or cached photo/document content without a forward header.
copy_message.returns: Native Message for the newly sent copy.
notes: Protected content is rejected. Service messages, polls, games and other unsupported copy shapes fail explicitly. File references are not refreshed automatically.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

create_channel.summary: Create a broadcast channel and return its uniquely identified server entity.
notes: Not retried on uncertain outcome. Bot/account restrictions and ownership rules remain Telegram decisions.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

create_supergroup.summary: Create a megagroup, optionally with forum topics enabled.
create_supergroup.returns: Native Channel with the server megagroup fields.
create_supergroup.example: group = await client.create_supergroup("Discussion", about="Project chat", forum=True)
notes: Forum is a creation flag, not an automatic migration of an existing basic group. Creation ambiguity raises SerializationError.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

create_group.summary: Resolve user references and create a basic group with explicit invitees.
create_group.returns: Native Chat from the actual creation result.
notes: Requires 1–200 user references. Returned creation does not guarantee that privacy-restricted invitees were admitted; inspect the raw result if missing-invitee details are needed.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

create_chat_invite_link.summary: Create an invite using the existing export_invite_link implementation.
notes: A familiar creation name over the existing supported operation, with the same expiry, approval and usage constraints.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

revoke_chat_invite_link.summary: Revoke a supplied real Telegram invite URL without removing current members.
notes: Requires a https://t.me/ invite URL and server permission. Permanent-link revocation may return replacement metadata.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

get_chat_invite_link.summary: Read the exported link available in full-chat metadata without creating one.
get_chat_invite_link.returns: str or None when no exported link is exposed.
notes: None represents absent/unavailable metadata, not successful link creation. Server admin/privacy restrictions still apply.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

delete_bot_commands.summary: Reset commands in one bot-command scope and language.
notes: Does not erase other languages/scopes automatically. None scope uses BotCommandScopeDefault.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

get_chat_menu_button.summary: Fetch the bot menu for a user or the default user scope.
notes: None user means the default menu scope, not an unknown account. This is a bot-only server capability.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

set_chat_menu_button.summary: Set a default/user bot menu to a Web App, commands menu or Telegram default.
notes: Supply both text and HTTPS URL for a Web App. commands=True is mutually exclusive with Web App fields; no fields selects BotMenuButtonDefault.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

get_inline_bot_results.summary: Resolve a bot and destination and retrieve server inline results.
notes: Familiar direct entry point for get_inline_results; pagination offset is an opaque server string.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

send_inline_bot_result.summary: Send a real inline result using its server query identity and result ID.
send_inline_bot_result.returns: Native Message correlated to the send response.
notes: Use a nonempty result set and real server-provided query/result IDs. No access hash, result ID or inline payload is fabricated.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

delete_chat_photo.summary: Remove a basic-group/channel photo through its appropriate endpoint.
notes: Sends InputChatPhotoEmpty explicitly and does not upload a zero-byte file. Server permissions remain mandatory.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

set_chat_photo.summary: Upload and set a basic-group/channel photo without manual TL construction.
notes: User peers are rejected before upload. Existing transfer ownership, validation and cancellation rules apply.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

set_profile_photo.summary: Upload and set a still account profile photo.
set_profile_photo.returns: Native photos.Photo containing server photo/user metadata.
notes: Does not add profile videos or configure another bot profile. Server account restrictions and file/DC limits apply.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

get_profile_photos.summary: Collect visible user profile photos with bounded server paging.
notes: Limit is finite, 0–10000; pages are at most 100. Zero makes no request. User photo history is distinct from a channel photo.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

delete_profile_photos.summary: Delete explicit native account photo references using their actual hashes.
notes: Accepts 1–100 Photo/InputPhoto values from real metadata. Integer IDs alone cannot manufacture required access/file references.
Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

download_profile_photo.summary: Fetch visible full profile metadata and download the largest supported photo size.

edit_message_reply_markup.summary: Replace message keyboard markup without editing text.

async for message in client.iter_messages("me", limit=100, page_size=50):

is_bot.summary: Inspect the authorized server identity to determine whether it is a bot.

send_cached_media.summary: Reuse server photo/document metadata without reupload or foreign file-ID decoding.

send_media_group.summary: Upload and send a real photo/document album with per-item captions and response correlation.

from gramflux import AlbumItem
messages = await client.send_media_group("me", [AlbumItem("one.jpg", "First"), AlbumItem("two.jpg", "Second")])

send_video_note.summary: Upload/send a round MP4 video note with explicit square dimensions.

send_venue.summary: Build and send a geographic venue with title, address and optional provider metadata.

Requires a connected authorized account unless only a known identity is handled locally. Server RPC errors, deadlines and cancellation propagate; ambiguous writes are not automatically retried.

send_game.summary: Send a registered bot game using an actual bot reference and short name.

filters.chat.summary: Select events whose marked chat ID equals any supplied numeric ID.
filters.chat.notes: No usernames, I/O or peer resolution occurs. Compose with sender/text predicates using &, | and ~.

filters.sender.summary: Select events from one of the supplied sender IDs.
filters.sender.notes: Use actual known account IDs. A sender filter does not restrict the chat unless a chat predicate is also composed.

filters.regex.summary: Compile a Python regular expression and search event text.

filters.command.summary: Match command names in the first token with explicit prefix and optional bot address.

filters.data.summary: Compare callback payload bytes exactly with the provided value.

filters.update_type.summary: Select one or more exact native Update constructor classes through the raw event route.

buttons.callback.summary: Build a native callback button with a visible label and bounded payload.

buttons.url.summary: Build a native button that opens a URL.

buttons.article.summary: Build a native inline article whose selected result sends literal text.

article = buttons.article("intro", "Introduction", "Hello", description="Read the introduction")
await client.answer_inline_query(event.query_id, [article])
buttons.article.notes: A result ID must be 1–64 UTF-8 bytes. Title/listing description and sent text are separate. Telegram enforces account, result and formatting rules.

Session.open.summary: Select an existing GramFlux session, normally requiring completed account authorization.
Session.open.returns: Session intent object; the file is opened at Client.connect, not at factory call time.
Session.open.example:
session = Session.open("account", require_authorized=False)
async with Client(session, api_id=api_id, api_hash=api_hash) as client:
    await client.login()
Session.open.notes: False permits pending login reuse; it does not bypass Telegram authentication. Missing files and foreign session formats fail explicitly.

Session.create.summary: Select exclusive creation of a new named persistent session.
Session.create.returns: Session intent object; creation/locking happens during Client.connect.
Session.create.example:
session = Session.create("account")
async with Client(session, api_id=api_id, api_hash=api_hash) as client:
    await client.login()
Session.create.notes: An existing file raises SessionAlreadyExists. Do not delete an authenticated or partially authorized session just to bypass that error.

Session.temporary.summary: Select in-memory storage with no session file.
Session.temporary.returns: Session intent object for process-local MemoryStorage.
Session.temporary.example:
async with Client(Session.temporary(), api_id=api_id, api_hash=api_hash) as client:
    await client.login()
Session.temporary.notes: Process exit loses local state, including pending login. Disconnect does not automatically revoke the remote Telegram authorization.

event_fields.message: Native Message or MessageService associated with the event. Payload repr is redacted; reading text/media is still sensitive application data.
event_fields.edited: False for new-message events; True for edits. It reflects event routing, not whether every field has changed.
event_fields.client: Bound Client used by event reply/edit/delete/download/answer helpers. Detached events can have None; helpers then raise LifecycleError.
event_fields.chat_type: private, group or channel when the message peer can be classified; None when unavailable. Basic groups and supergroups are not collapsed into an invented wire type.
event_fields.update: Actual accepted native Update object. Counter/gap validation happens before dispatch; this is not a fabricated wrapper around every recovered Message.
event_fields.message_ids: Tuple of deleted message IDs. Global non-channel IDs may arrive without an identifiable chat.
event_fields.chat_id: Marked chat identity when known. Non-channel deletion and inline callback events may have None; never guess the peer from a global message ID.
event_fields.max_id: Read-history cursor reported by Telegram. It does not mean the application processed every callback up to this ID.
event_fields.outbox: True for an outgoing-history read update; False for inbox read state.
event_fields.sender_id: Account ID associated with the author/query/status update when available. This is not automatically a complete User object.
event_fields.status: Native UserStatus variant. Last-seen visibility and online state are governed by Telegram privacy rules.
event_fields.query_id: Query identity to use when answering the callback/inline event. It is distinct from message_id and from an MTProto message ID.
event_fields.data: Optional callback payload bytes; can be None for game/other callback shapes. No automatic UTF-8/JSON decoding is performed.
event_fields.message_id: Ordinary message ID for a chat callback, when present. For inline callbacks, inspect inline_message_id instead.
event_fields.inline_message_id: Native inline-message identifier for inline callbacks. It is separate from chat_id/message_id and may be None for ordinary callbacks.
event_fields.game_short_name: Optional game identifier when the callback is game-related; it is not a URL or a replacement for callback data.
event_fields.query: Literal inline search query submitted by the user. Do not log it without an application privacy decision.
event_fields.offset: Opaque inline-query pagination cursor. It is not a byte offset or a numeric page index.

config_fields.request_timeout: Finite positive request deadline in seconds, including time waiting for request admission. Also bounds complete initial connection/auth-key setup. It is not a limit on the lifetime of the Client or all pagination pages together.
config_fields.max_concurrent_requests: Positive integer application RPC admission bound. It does not spawn this many event workers. Native liveness traffic has reserved bounded capacity.
config_fields.event_queue_size: Positive integer count setting for event/native receive queues. Slow handlers can trigger bounded backpressure/overflow; the receiver does not silently discard updates.
config_fields.reconnect_attempts: Nonnegative integer bound for initial TCP establishment retries. It does not replay pending application writes or provide transparent in-flight reconnection.
config_fields.peer_cache_size: Integer from 1 through 4096. Bounds account-local entity/access-hash metadata; default 2048. A cache entry is not permanent proof of username ownership.
config_fields.transport: One of full, intermediate or abridged. All use the same native MTProto 2.0 encryption. Proxy/HTTP/WebSocket/obfuscated transports are not exposed by this setting.
config_fields.update_queue_bytes: Positive queued-update budget measured by uncompressed TL body byte sizes; default 16 MiB. It is not a cap on Python object heap size or total RSS.
